How We Set Our Daily NBA Lineups

Our staff sets the expected daily lineups 24-30 hours before tip-off. The expected lineups are then tweaked throughout the day of the game.

Lineups are only confirmed when an official NBA source provides that information.

Unfortunately, the NBA does not require that starting lineups be submitted before tipoff, which is why we are sometimes limited to waiting until a game tips off to accurately pass on who is starting for some games. Also, sometimes players are "scratched" at the very last minute.

If a player has a color bar next to his name, that reflects some level of uncertainty about whether he'll be active for the game. Most players have a color bar when dealing with an injury, but we will also add estimates if a player's status in doubt due to rest or other off-court issues.

NBA Starting Lineups

NBA starting lineups are one of the most important factors when it comes to drafting and setting your fantasy basketball and NBA DFS lineups. The starting lineup helps you gauge what players are in line to play the most minutes, which equates to greater production and ending your fantasy matchup with more points.

Be sure to get started and set your fantasy basketball lineup with RotoWire's NBA starting lineups that is updated on a daily basis.

How to Use NBA Starting Lineups for Fantasy Basketball

NBA lineups are of utmost importance for basketball fantasy owners. For example, if LeBron James is OUT of the starting lineup, fantasy basketball owners are not going to want to have him in their lineup for that game. Instead they will want to replace him with someone who is playing that day. In addition, a player may show up on the NBA injury report which can affect their status when it comes to the NBA starting lineups.

Why NBA Lineups is Important for NBA DFS

NBA lineups also affect the NBA DFS landscape as well. Whenever you have a star player out on a team, your DFS lineups may want to target other players from the same team, as they will be seeing more action and have improved statistics for that particular game.

NBA Projected Minutes To Help You In Fantasy Basketball

At RotoWire, we have rolled out a new feature called "Projected Minutes" as you can see on this page. What this does is has our projected minutes for each player, giving you an edge on just how many minutes a player on NBA depth charts is expected to play. For NBA projections models, DFS, player props, and other forms of NBA gaming, projected minutes is one of the key elements of understanding and predicting potential outcomes.
